Warlord: Awaji is an immersive first-person strategy game in which you assume the role of a samurai commander and personally lead your army to conquer Awaji Island. You must manage your troops, build a camp, capture settlements and fortifications, manage conquered lands, and simultaneously engage in battles with your own hands. Here, army command is closely tied to the actions of the hero himself: while your troops carry out your orders, you can directly enter the battlefield and change the course of the conflict in real time.

Conquest of Awaji

The island is a vast open world, modeled on the real-life Awaji, complete with numerous temples and shrines. Peaceful caravans and warrior squads constantly move along the roads, so the situation can change even during your journey. Local clans react to your actions, forcing you to plan your attacks and choose your targets in advance. Capturing strongholds weakens enemy forces, while controlling rival altars increases your spiritual power. Warrior monks offer additional abilities, capable of casting curses and assisting in coordinated attacks.

The army gradually becomes the primary tool for expanding your domain. You can recruit samurai, develop commanders, and create your own battle formations through a user-friendly menu. Each soldier has a name and personal combat experience, which grows through participation in battles. The best warriors can be equipped with more powerful weapons and armor, and the combination of infantry, ranged units, and cavalry allows you to tailor your army to the specific situation.
